findings.reason: a worker reproducing or re-measuring §49 will materialise the named revision `f42dad3b0` while the only kept profile was taken at `da1a110ab`, so the section's evidence and its stated base disagree and the literal must be corrected (either to `da1a110ab`, or the profile re-taken at `f42dad3b0`).
findings.text: §49 says the coordinator profiled the warm call "at `f42dad3b0`" but names the profile log `~/.cache/reckon-read-deadline/roadmap-profile-*.log`, and that log is `roadmap-profile-da1a110ab.log`; the directory's own convention encodes the profiled revision in the file name (cf. `runs-view-profile-24f4416db.log`, cited by §48 as "at `24f4416db`"), and `da1a110ab` is a different commit from `f42dad3b0` (17:56 vs 17:48 today)

findings.reason: the gate as written measures the limit that will not bind and can pass while the process count hits the limit that will, so the section's own condition ("report blocked rather than shipping a watch that fails") is not reachable through the check it names; the one-line fix is to measure watches *and* instances per process against both files.
findings.text: the ship gate says "report the number of sessions they allow against `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches` (976,038 on the fleet node today). If the limit cannot hold the sessions a fleet runs, report blocked", but the per-user resource a fleet of long-lived watching processes exhausts first is the inotify *instance* count, not the watch count: `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances` reads 128 on this host against 976,038 watches, so a fleet of tens of coordinator sessions each holding its own MCP watch plus the served process can hit the instance ceiling while the watches consumed stay far below 976,038 and the gate reports the fleet fits

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every cited symbol and file resolves (serve.py, mcp.py, `_store.py`, `served_code.py`, all seven gate tests, the profile log), but the revision the section attributes to its own profile is not the revision the log names.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the done-when's negative control and per-assertion counts are present and measurable, but the ship gate on the watch count names only `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches` and so cannot show the failure its own text guards against.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate arms log "under the run directory" with a revision header and an `EXIT=` tail, the evidence fragment has an explicit write path, and the profile is kept on a durable path under `~/.cache/reckon-read-deadline/` (realised as `roadmap-profile-da1a110ab.log`), not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags appear in the new symbol or file names (`tests/test_a_warm_mcp_read_reuses_its_walk.py`, the factored opt-in function); no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — checked all three. (a) The stated cause matches the cited evidence: the profile log shows the two callers the section names (`_discovery_signature` ×2 at 12.54 s and `_reuse_covered` ×3 at 7.44 s) accounting for nearly all of the 14.40 s of stat time. (b) The mechanism produces the done-when: dropping `_SIGNATURE_TTL_S` to 0 makes `_discovery_signature` walk, and setting it to the served TTL with the memo dropped on write is what makes the "no stat inside the window" and "own write seen by next read" assertions reachable. (c) The mechanism runs on the real code path with callers named: `_fresh_discovery` (`reckon/serve.py:1375`) consumes the signature, `write_plan` is reached by every MCP plan-state writer, and the child process path is named through `SERVED_CHILD_PROGRAM`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §49 has one goal, opting the MCP process (and its served child) into the existing reuse window behind the change watch; the write-invalidation hook and the child opt-in are parts of that one change, not separate deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s31: [s46, s49]`, so §31 waits on §49 as the section's last sentence states, and the earlier finding (s31 and s49 both writing `reckon/serve.py` with no ordering) is resolved; every declared edge resolves to an existing section.
